references.text: Bezer in the wilderness, in the plateau, for the Reubenites; Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites. Jahzah is mentioned here as one of the cities within the territory of the tribe of Reuben.
Jahzah and Kedemoth are listed as Levitical cities given to the Merarites from the tribe of Reuben, confirming that these cities were allocated to Reuben.
Jahzah is noted as the place where Israel defeated Sihon, king of the Amorites, in battle. This provides the historical background for why the city became part of Israelite territory.
Sihon and all his people marched out against Israel to fight at Jahzah. This verse refers to the same battle that gave Israel control over this area.
Jeremiah prophesies judgment against Jahzah as one of the cities in the plateau of Moab, showing the city's geographical location and later fate.
Kedemoth is mentioned as one of the Levitical cities in the territory of the tribe of Reuben, consistent with Joshua's allocation.
